questions: What papers study capability degradation or 'brain rot' during continual pretraining / domain-adaptive pretraining on low-quality short text (e.g., social media), and what mechanisms do they propose?
What prior work analyzes per-sequence vs per-token loss normalization (token weighting) for variable-length sequence training in language modeling or seq2seq, and what are known biases/failure modes?
What papers discuss sequence packing for LLM training and its side effects (e.g., cross-contamination / attention masking), beyond pure efficiency gains?

Which papers discuss length bias from per-sentence (per-sequence) loss normalization in language modeling or neural machine translation training, and propose token-level or length-aware weighting as a fix?

What prior work studies how packing/concatenation changes the effective context distribution during training (e.g., cross-document attention vs intra-document masking) and its impact on generalization/long-context ability?

What prior work studies catastrophic forgetting or capability degradation during continual pretraining / domain-adaptive pretraining of language models, and what mitigation techniques (data mixing, replay, regularization) are proposed?
Are there papers analyzing how the number of optimizer updates (for a fixed token budget) affects model drift/forgetting in language model pretraining or continual pretraining?
What papers propose token-based batching or loss normalization to ensure equal per-token contribution when training on variable-length sequences in Transformers/LLMs?
